faq.a: Walid is associated with the Arabic form وَلِيد, whose core sense is walid; newborn, child.

faq.q: What is the origin of Walid?
faq.a: Walid is associated with Arabic. Walid is Arabic وَلِيد (Walīd), meaning 'newborn, child'.
Yes — the underlying form وَلِيد is Arabic.
Walid can occur in Muslim naming contexts, but it is better described as a Arabic-origin name used within some Muslim naming traditions than as an exclusively Islamic religious term.
Walid should not be classified as a Quranic personal name without a direct Quranic basis. The root و ل د is Quranic, but Walīd is not itself a Quranic personal name.

faq.q: What does Walid mean in Urdu?
faq.a: In Urdu, Walid is rendered ولید and carries the sense ولید، نومولود.

faq.q: What does Walid mean in Persian?
faq.a: In Persian, Walid is rendered ولید and carries the sense ولید، نوزاد.
A romanized syllable approximation is wa-lid. No IPA transcription is asserted because a verified phonetic transcription was not available.

faq.q: What are the variants of Walid?
faq.a: Romanization variants include Walid, walid. Script forms are ولید, وَلِيد, वलीद.

faq.q: Is Walid a boy's or girl's name?
faq.a: Documented usage records this form as male. Gender is not inferred from the meaning of the word, and actual use may vary between communities.
